about: Force-driven scenarios for consolidation and reverse discovery, the two modes shared by all four skills through references/migrating-decisions.md. Each scenario names what the repository looks like and what a correct run must therefore produce. There is no numeric scoring: a run passes when it reaches the stated outcome for the stated reason.

criteria.statement: Only paths or code scopes the user explicitly confirmed influence anything written. A candidate list may be shown; nothing on it is used until confirmed.
A duplicate, overlap, or contradiction is reported as a finding or a candidate. No run auto-merges, auto-supersedes, or silently drops one side.
No existing ADR or decision file's prose is edited or deleted. Superseding an existing file only ever happens through a newly proposed decision, never by editing the old one.
Every confirmed input appears in the traceability report exactly once, with a disposition and, where required, a reason.
Every rule reverse discovery proposes starts at verification: narrative. Raising it is never done in the same run.
Every generated decision is status: proposed. The constitution is unaffected until a human runs promote.
No percentage, coverage number, or maturity score appears anywhere in a migration report or its summary.
When more than 20 decisions would be warranted, the run ranks and states what was left out, rather than proposing all of them or silently truncating without saying so.

scenarios.forces: docs/adr/ holds six prose ADRs. The user confirms three of them for migration.

expect.notes: Only the three confirmed files are read or referenced. The other three are never mentioned as migrated, merged, or superseded — they simply don't appear, because they were never confirmed.

scenarios.forces: The user says "just migrate everything in docs/adr/."

expect.notes: The run declines to treat the whole directory as confirmed, lists the candidates, and asks which ones to include.

scenarios.forces: Two confirmed prose ADRs, migrated into two schema decisions, end up with overlapping scope globs on rules that read as contradictory.

expect.notes: The traceability report names both decisions and both rules as a candidate conflict. Neither file's status is set to superseded automatically.

scenarios.forces: A confirmed prose ADR is migrated into a new schema decision.

expect.notes: The original prose ADR file is byte-identical afterward. It is not deleted, converted, or reformatted.

scenarios.forces: Every file the user confirms already parses as a schema decision.

expect.notes: The run says there is nothing to migrate and still writes a traceability report — every input disposed as its own existing decision, none newly proposed.

scenarios.forces: The user asks for a baseline for src/domain/**. 47 of 51 files avoid importing infra directly; 4 do not.

expect.notes: A narrative rule is proposed, its Context names the count and lists all four exceptions by path. Nothing is deterministic or review at proposal time.

scenarios.forces: The user asks for a baseline for a small, inconsistent utility script directory with no discernible regularity.

expect.notes: The run reports it found nothing worth proposing and writes no decision. This is a correct outcome, not a failure.

scenarios.forces: A large undocumented monorepo where a thorough pass would justify 35 decisions.

expect.notes: The run proposes at most 20, ranked, and the report states which 15+ were left out and why, rather than proposing all 35 or silently stopping at 20 unexplained.

scenarios.forces: A migration run completes with 8 proposed decisions.

expect.notes: The constitution is byte-unchanged immediately after the run. A later, explicit promote of 2 of the 8 changes only those two rules' presence in the constitution.

scenarios.forces: A greenfield decide-architecture run reaches a recommendation.

expect.notes: Exactly one file is written under the decisions directory. No file is written to docs/adr/ for this new decision.
